verdict.rationale: First-party docs point developers to the open-source Python library for running a local agent, and the README frames it as usable from your own code with any LLM. Community users confirm that running locally connects the agent to their real browser and user profile. The 'without any cloud account' part is only implied by the library being open source; no first-party evidence states it, and local-browser setup docs are thin. Missing for 10: explicit first-party statement that no Browser Use Cloud account or API key is needed locally, in-depth first-party docs on connecting to a local browser.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the agent against a local browser on my own machine for development, without any cloud account

citations.quote: For a local agent, use the [open-source library](/open-source/quickstart).
Want to automate the web at scale, from your own code, and with any LLM? Use the Python library
If you run it locally, you can connect it to your real browser and user profile where you are already logged in.
Documentation for Browser Use Cloud Agent and Browser APIs, and the separate open-source Python library
